summary: Ukrainian forces conducted a second strike on the Crimean Bridge on November 17, destroying the automobile arch span with an FP-5 Flamingo missile and halting all traffic, culminating a month-long seven-stage operation using 12 indigenous drone and missile types. Russia responded with a massive overnight barrage of over 50 Shahed/Geran-5 and jet drones plus cruise missiles targeting 12 Ukrainian regions, damaging energy infrastructure near Kyiv. A Russian Shahed drone violated Moldovan airspace over Chisinau, forcing a national airspace closure, while Russian military aircraft violated Japanese airspace prompting fighter scrambles.

Russia launched a massive overnight barrage of 50+ Shahed/Geran-5 and jet drones from 10+ launch areas targeting 12 Ukrainian regions, alongside cruise missiles striking Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78404, @mon1tor_ua/78411)
Russian cruise missiles damaged energy infrastructure in Bila Tserkva and Boryspil districts near Kyiv, continuing systematic targeting of the Ukrainian power grid. (Source: @eRadarrua/131340)
A Russian Shahed drone penetrated Moldovan airspace over Chisinau twice, forcing full national airspace closure and diversion of international civilian flights. (Source: @eRadarrua/131358)
Russian military aircraft violated Japanese airspace near Okinoerabu for three minutes, transited the Tsushima Strait, and were tracked by South Korea and Taiwan. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24009)
A Russian military aircraft crashed in the Kemerovo region. (Source: @UkraineNow/85359)

points: Ukrainian forces executed a second strike on the Crimean Bridge on November 17 using an FP-5 Flamingo missile that destroyed the automobile arch span and damaged the railway deck, stopping all road, rail, and maritime traffic through the Kerch Strait. The strike concluded a month-long, seven-stage SBU operation that first degraded Russian air defenses before employing 12 distinct Ukrainian-made weapons including Palianytsia, Neptune, Ruta, Dovbush, Vendetta, Da Vinci, Sich, Mich-2000, AN-197, FP-1, Flamingo, and R-360 Neptune missiles. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24007, @DeepStateUA/24005, @UkraineNow/85355)

Ukraine demonstrated an indigenous communication and targeting system that guided a drone swarm via real-time video links directly to missiles without reliance on Starlink or Starshield, marking the first operational use of autonomous relay networks for precision strike on strategic infrastructure. (Source: @eRadarrua/131389)

Ukrainian air defenses engaged a massive Russian drone wave across multiple regions; air raid alerts sounded in Kyiv (Desnyanskyi district), Chernihiv, Vinnytsia, Kirovohrad, Dnipropetrovsk, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Cherkasy, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi, Ivano-Frankivsk, Zakarpattia, and Volyn, with monitoring channels reporting numerous jet and strike drone groups. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78410, @mon1tor_ua/78415, @eRadarrua/131335, @eRadarrua/131368, @eRadarrua/131391, @eRadarrua/131392)

President Zelensky confirmed that Palianytsia drones struck the automobile section, while Neptune missiles, Ruta and FP-5 drones hit the railway section, and the Flamingo missile conducted a guided strike on the bridge structure. (Source: @UkraineNow/85355)

Russia launched a massive combined drone and missile attack overnight November 17, deploying over 50 Shahed/Geran-5 and jet drones from at least 10 launch areas including Bryansk, Kursk, occupied Crimea, and Russian-occupied Ukrainian regions, targeting 12 Ukrainian oblasts: Kyiv, Chernihiv, Vinnytsia, Kirovohrad, Dnipropetrovsk, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Cherkasy, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi, Ivano-Frankivsk, Zakarpattia, and Volyn. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78404, @mon1tor_ua/78411, @mon1tor_ua/78412, @kpszsu/96996, @kpszsu/96970, @kpszsu/96982, @kpszsu/97000, @kpszsu/96980, @kpszsu/96995, @kpszsu/96993, @kpszsu/96968, @kpszsu/96966, @kpszsu/96972)

Russian cruise missiles struck Dnipro/Kamianske and Zaporizhzhia, while missile or drone impacts damaged energy infrastructure objects in Bila Tserkva and Boryspil districts of Kyiv region. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78379, @mon1tor_ua/78382, @eRadarrua/131340)

A Russian Shahed-type drone violated Moldovan airspace twice, entering from Odesa region toward Tiraspol, returning, then crossing again near Malaiesti, and flying directly over Chisinau (Botanica area, city gates, circus) before Moldova closed its entire airspace at 16:27, diverting passenger flights from Yerevan, Istanbul, and Sharm el-Sheikh to Romanian airspace. (Source: @eRadarrua/131358)

Two probable Russian military aircraft violated Japanese airspace near Okinoerabu island (Fukuoka prefecture) for approximately three minutes each, prompting Japan to scramble fighters, issue warnings, and lodge a formal protest; the aircraft then transited the Tsushima Strait, flew between Yonaguni and Taiwan, and exited into the Pacific, with South Korea and Taiwan also detecting and tracking the same formation. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24009)
A Russian military aircraft crashed in the Kemerovo region. (Source: @UkraineNow/85359)

Jet drones were observed over Dnipro city, Yurivka, and two jet drones flew past Izium in the direction of the front line, indicating continued Russian aerial reconnaissance and strike activity in the Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv sectors. (Source: @eRadarrua/131387)

Russian jet drones targeted Dnipropetrovsk region including Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih, and Pavlohrad, with monitoring channels reporting multiple groups in the area. (Source: @kpszsu/96966, @mon1tor_ua/78412)

A jet drone passed near Velyka Dymerka moving toward Brovary/Kyiv. (Source: @kpszsu/96970)
A Geran-5 missile from Bryansk region targeted Chernihiv district; another Geran-5 from Chernihiv region targeted Vyshhorod district (Kyiv region). (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78412)
